summary: Yasuo Matsunami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Taisho University, where he was taught by Ryukai Mano in 1979 and served as a researcher (attested 1995–2006). Until 2010, he was an advisor at Sravakabhumi Kenkyukai.
Yasuo Sano is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied under Tetsuro Watsuji at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1973) and held posts at the University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

Yasuro Abe is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako and Otani universities. He held academic positions at Osaka, Otemae, and Nagoya universities, later serving at Nichibunken and Ryukoku University.
Yasusaburo Sakaki (1870–1929) studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1895 to 1899. He later held academic appointments at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1906) and Kyushu University (~1906–1925).

Yasutaka Muroya works in Indology and philosophy. He was a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and Leipzig University (attested 2015), and became a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Tohoku University. He held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1978–2002) and Koyasan University (~2002–2012), and served as president of the Society of Esoteric Buddhism (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Yang studied for an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).
Yeshe Thupten is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1982, he was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia and held a post at Middlebury College.
Yeshi Dhonden (1927–2019) worked in Tibetology. He studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. In 1961, he founded Men-Tsee-Khang, serving as its director until 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner.

Yifa is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. She held posts at University of the West (~1996–2004) and Harvard (2001–2002), and founded the Woodenfish Foundation.

Yigal Bronner is an Indology scholar who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1995–1999). He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2008).

Yijie Tang (1927–2014) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Peking University (~1947–1951), he taught there as a professor (~1956–2014), served at Stanford (~1990–1991), and founded the International Academy of Chinese Culture.

Yiliang Zhou (1913–2001) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Fu Jen, Yenching, and Harvard universities, as well as under Yinke Chen, and served as a professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).

Yin Shun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan, Wuchang, and Taisho University, and under Taixu. He taught at Minnan, Wuchang, and Fawang Buddhist institutes, and served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

Ying-shih Yü (1930–2021) was a historian, sinologist, and philosopher. He studied at Yenching, New Asia College, CUHK, and Harvard. He held professorships at Michigan, Harvard, CUHK, Yale (1977–1987), Princeton (1987–2001), and Cornell (1991–1992).

Yingguang Qu (1883–1973) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School and trained under teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Bai Puren, Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche.

Yinke Chen (1890–1969) was a historian, sinologist, and linguist. He studied at Humboldt, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard under Lanman, Lüders, Müller, and Haenisch. He held professorships at Tsinghua, Peking, HKU, Yenching, Lingnan, and Sun Yat-sen universities.
Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935–2018) was a philosophy scholar. He was educated at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957–1968), and Princeton University (~1966–1968).
